html:
SMTO-BOOT-0002 — SMTO can't start with one of the options or settings given

GUID: 120c8ced-2a22-4f67-b60d-9c85d39e7707
Slug: boot-option-invalid
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • A command was started with an option SMTO doesn't know, or with a value it can't accept, such as a data folder that doesn't exist. SMTO stopped at that point instead of guessing what you meant.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Compare what you typed with the Usage line printed under this error. It lists every option this command accepts. Fix any typo or remove options it doesn't list. Most of these stops come from a typo or an option meant for a different command, such as a Gateway option given to ./startup.sh.
  2. If the message mentions --data-dir, check that the folder exists and its path is typed correctly, then start again. SMTO refuses a data folder that doesn't exist so it never starts with a new, empty one by mistake.
  3. If someone set SMTO settings in the environment or a start file, ask them to check the values; on/off settings accept only true, false, 1 or 0. SMTO checks these values when it starts and refuses anything outside the allowed range.

What success looks like

  • The command runs without this error, and SMTO or the Gateway begins starting up.

If it still fails

  • Copy the exact command you ran and the full terminal message, including the Error reference line, and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't point --data-dir at a new empty folder to get past this; SMTO would start without your existing data.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A launcher, installer or operator command rejected an unknown option or an unusable value, such as a nonexistent --data-dir, a non-boolean AOR_LLM_BUDGET_GROWTH_* value, a checkpoint CPU fraction outside (0, 1], an invalid palette URL or recovery generation.

What this means

  • Entry-point parsing rejects an unsupported option/value, including invalid palette URL, boolean configuration, generation selector or writer-budget fraction. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Entry-point parsing rejects an unsupported option/value, including invalid palette URL, boolean configuration, generation selector or writer-budget fraction.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the actual option/value and owning entry point instead of assuming every occurrence is an unknown flag.

How to fix it

  • Read the flag named in the technical detail and compare it with the entry point's usage line: startup.sh accepts --config, --data-dir (existing directory), --host, --port, --manual-port, --reload and --https; Gateway startup.sh accepts --host, --port, --instance, --server-host, --server-port, --server-scheme, --trace-commands and reset. Also check environment values: AOR_LLM_BUDGET_GROWTH_* and AOR_LLM_FORCE_THINKING_BUDGET must be true/false/1/0, AOR_CONTROLLER_CHECKPOINT_CPU_FRACTION must be in (0, 1], aor palette --url must be an http(s) base URL without credentials, query or fragment, recovery --generation must be current or previous, and install-vllm.sh takes exactly one environment name.
  • Correct the reported option or value against the exact entry point's usage and configuration contract.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The documented command/configuration input passes its specific validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
